transcript.text:
SailPoint ISC uses the **OAuth2 client credentials** flow. POST to your tenant's token endpoint with the PAT credentials in the form body.

## curl

```bash
curl -X POST "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}"
```

## Python (requests)

```python
import requests

tenant = "your-org"
client_id = "your-client-id"
client_secret = "your-client-secret"

response = requests.post(
    f"https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token",
    data={
        "grant_type": "client_credentials",
        "client_id": client_id,
        "client_secret": client_secret,
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()
access_token = response.json()["access_token"]
```

## Using the token

Pass it as a Bearer token on subsequent requests:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer {access_token}" \
  "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts"
```

**Notes:**
- Replace `{tenant}` with your org name (e.g., `acme` → `acme.api.identitynow.com`).
- The returned `access_token` is a short-lived JWT (typically 30–60 minutes). Cache it and refresh when it expires rather than fetching a new one on every call.
- No `scope` parameter is required for PAT-based client credentials; the token inherits the scopes granted when the PAT was created in the ISC UI.

```answer-summary
    path: /oauth/token
    api_version: oauth
auth_flow: OAuth2 client credentials

```
